rationale: M59.A7 (#825). Zig emitted NO line_number on any relationship before this pin — measured through the production entry on a 200-file draw of the zig corpus: 0 of 20,789 edges lined (validation/m59/results/oracle-callsite-scoped-zig-f200.json now reads 20,789/20,789 lined, INCONSISTENT 0). The pre-fix state is therefore 'unlined', and the three traps below are the ways a zig line can be PRESENT and still wrong, each measured in the source before being written here: (1) a wrapped @import — the `const std =` declaration starts on 18 while the module path literal is written on 19, so a construct-start line stamps the import one line early; (2) a wrapped field access — a `field_expression` starts at its RECEIVER, so `counters` on 39 and `.misses` on 40 report 39 unless the LEAF node is used (the same class the c lane measured on a newline-continued function-pointer call); (3) a wrapped parameter type — the `pub fn seed(` keyword is on 30 while `Counters` is written on 31. The forbidRelationships entries are exactly those pre-fix positions, so re-introducing any of them fails the gate instead of passing silently.

forbidRelationships.note: pre-fix shape: the `const std =` declaration line; the @import path is written on 19
pre-fix shape: the container's own start line; `hits` is declared on 22
pre-fix shape: the `pub fn seed(` keyword line; the type is written on 31
pre-fix shape / fabricated-substitute class: the enclosing assignment's line; the read is written on 35 (the line-34 mention is a WRITE, correctly emitted as no edge at all)
pre-fix shape: the field_expression's RECEIVER line; the leaf `.misses` is written on 40
